question: Do the two arms start from the same Git tree (content), despite different recorded commit hashes?
method: Re-create each fixture's initial/ as a git repo (cp -r initial/. ; git add -A ; git commit) and compare blob-tree hashes. The original fixture dirs are the frozen byte source.
content_level_conclusion: identical tree per sample (arms share content)
reason_original_unresolvable: The run's base repo lived in a TemporaryDirectory (e.g. /tmp/tmpcugnc8bx) that was deleted; `git cat-file -t <recorded_head>` fails for all four recorded hashes. The differing commit hashes therefore cannot be independently resolved to trees from surviving data.
interpretation: Differing commit hashes are consistent with non-deterministic commit metadata (author/committer timestamp, since each arm created its own git repo at a different wall-clock time). Content-level proof shows the same fixture bytes produce the same tree; but the original commit objects are gone, so the 'same initial version' claim is supported at content level and marked UNKNOWN at the original-commit-object level (not asserted as byte-proven for the deleted run).
